entities.summary:
Guillermo Raimundo de Vich y de Vallterra was a cardinal in the Catholic Church from 1519 to 1525. He played a key role in the governance of the church during a tumultuous period, marked by the Protestant Reformation and the rise of powerful noble families. De Vich's involvement with the papacy was significant, as he served under Pope Leo X and helped navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries between European monarchs.

De Vich's contributions to the church extend beyond his political influence, as he also played a role in promoting the arts and education during his tenure. He was particularly interested in supporting the work of artists and architects, which had significant implications for the development of Renaissance-era architecture and art.

Despite his importance within the Catholic Church, de Vich's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by other figures from this period. Nevertheless, his contributions to the church's governance and artistic endeavors remain an important part of its history.

The most striking aspect of de Vich's career is perhaps his association with the Inquisition, which he played a role in during his time as cardinal. This legacy continues to be felt today, with ongoing debates about the morality and effectiveness of such institutions.
